one_line: An 8-second selfie of a woman sipping a drink under the text 'a filter that shows how my future child will look', where a smiling toddler appears next to her and the image then flips to black and white as both stare at the camera.

hook.visual: Close selfie of a blonde woman in a striped multicolour knit sweater smiling over a fluted glass of a milky drink; the edge of a child's face peeks in at the left at 1.0s.
hook.on_screen_text: פילטר שמראה איך ייראה הילד העתידי שלי: (A filter that shows what my future child will look like:)
hook.why_it_stops_the_scroll: The Hebrew text states the whole premise in the first frame (observed), so the viewer immediately waits for the child to appear; the reveal arrives within 2 seconds (child fully visible at 2.0s), which is a very short open loop.

beats.observed: Woman in a striped knit sweater holds a ribbed glass of a beige drink at chin level and smiles at the phone camera, selfie angle, green plant at right. Small 'AI+' badge at top-left.
beats.spoken: No usable speech (transcript only has a one-line artifact).
beats.on_screen_text: פילטר שמראה איך ייראה הילד העתידי שלי:

beats.observed: She lowers the glass; a child's face enters at the far left edge, partly cropped, with blue eyes and light hair.

A toddler with blond hair and blue eyes is now fully in frame, smiling, leaning against her; she looks down at him fondly. The glass is now smooth (no ribs) and the sweater stripe layout looks different from 0.0s.
Image drops to black and white. Both turn to the camera with open mouths. A stacked skull and exploding-head emoji sticker appears over the glass.
Held black-and-white shot of both with the same open-mouthed expression; frames at 6.0, 7.0 and 8.0 are nearly identical, so the end looks frozen or very slow.

payoff: The child appears at 1.0 to 2.0s (fully visible at 2.0s); the black-and-white shocked-reaction beat lands at 5.0s and is held to the end.
cta: none (no spoken or written ask; the hashtags #aifilter and #Multiaverso point to a trend others can copy)
share_or_comment_trigger: Viewers who want to try the same filter on themselves, or friends tagged to see 'your future kid'. Only 23 comments against 162K views suggests it was watched and liked more than discussed.
why_it_worked: The premise is a single Hebrew line shown in frame 1 and the reveal comes in about 2 seconds, so the 8.5 s clip pays off almost immediately (162K views).
It rides a trend that viewers can copy (#aifilter, #Multiaverso in the caption), so 'what would mine look like' drives watching; 2,876 likes is a 1.78% like rate.
The black-and-white reaction beat at 5.0s changes the picture and adds an emoji reaction, giving a second small payoff after the reveal.
paid_signal: no: like_rate 1.78% is well above the 0.3% paid-looking threshold; account median is null so outlier_x cannot be computed.

solo_route.how: 1) Film a 4 to 5 second selfie of yourself sipping a drink and smiling at the camera, leaving room at the left of frame. 2) For the LumeBook version, take a still of a LumeBook illustrated child hero (fictional, no real child photo), turn it into a 3 second image-to-video clip of the child leaning into frame and smiling, and composite it in CapCut at 1.0s; or run the selfie through a face-based AI effect on your own face. 3) Put one Hebrew line on the first frame (the premise) and keep it for the whole clip. 4) At 5.0s switch to black and white, add one emoji sticker, and hold the last 3 seconds. Total about 8 seconds.
solo_route.needs: Nothing beyond your own face and LumeBook's own illustrations. Do not use a real child's photo without a parent's written consent. Label the child as AI or illustrated so it is not passed off as a real kid.

lumebook_version.hook_he: העליתי תמונה אחת ללומיבוק. ככה הילד נראה בספר:
lumebook_version.concept: A short selfie-style clip where the creator holds a drink, the LumeBook illustrated hero 'steps in' beside them, and the clip ends on a held reaction with the same one-line premise on screen. Show the real-to-illustrated likeness idea without using a real child's face.

evidence_notes: OBSERVED: text is quoted exactly as it appears; the badge reads 'AI+' (partly cut off by a dark corner) in every frame and is the only on-screen tool-like mark; no tool is named in text or caption beyond the hashtags #aifilter and #Multiaverso. AI-LOOKS (my read from frames, not certain): the child enters the frame from off-screen within one second; the glass changes from ribbed (0.0s) to smooth (2.0s); the sweater stripe layout is not the same at 0.0s and 2.0s; the whole clip desaturates at 5.0s; frames 6.0, 7.0 and 8.0 are almost identical. Skin looks soft but not obviously plastic, and the visible hand (dark nail polish) has a plausible finger count. I cannot tell whether the woman is real footage with an AI child added or the whole clip is AI-generated. SPOKEN: the transcript is a single 'תודה רבה.' (Thank you very much) over 0 to 2s with no matching mouth movement visible, so I treat it as a Whisper artifact over music and there is no usable speech. INFERRED: the account owner is the woman and the 'future child' is synthetic; the child has similar blond hair and blue eyes, consistent with a filter that blends the creator's features, but I cannot verify. LIKENESS/CONSENT: the child appears to be AI-generated, not a real minor, which lowers the consent risk; the risk for LumeBook is copying the trend with a real child's photo (needs parental consent) or presenting a synthetic child as real. made_by is 'unclear' because the schema has no 'creator's own account' value; it is a personal account that posted in first person.
